title: Trump & Xi Hug in China - BIG Grain Buying to Follow??

bullets: Grains lower: Dec corn −2.5c at 4.4425; Jan beans −4.25c at 12.2125; Dec SRW −9c at 5.8625; Dec KC −8.25c at 6.2475; Dec MPLS −3.75c at 6.36
Bloomberg: China unlikely to hit the $17B US ag purchase commitment by year-end (ample domestic supply, weak demand). Timeline may be extended
The September tariff cuts still aren’t in effect. Beijing never formally confirmed the $17B deal announced in May
Strong USD and weak BRL make US grain less competitive vs Brazil and Argentina
Trump and Xi met at APEC in Shenzhen. Xi pledged to oppose protectionism; Putin criticized Western sanctions ahead of a trilateral meeting
Joe: corn + SRW combined is about $10.42 vs a ~$19 peak in 2022. China could make political buys, as it did with beans, but that looks less likely as time passes
Corn and ethanol groups are lobbying for ethanol in maritime fuel at the UN IMO, which has no carbon-score framework for it yet
Current alcohol-capable ships could use ~2B gal/yr (~680M bu corn). With ships on order, that rises to 7.7B gal (~2.7B bu)
Ships burn ~90B gal of fuel a year. This is a much easier fix than SAF; Joe and Pete Meyer would lobby the shipping lines directly
Tue settles: Dec SRW +8c to ~5.95 and Dec HRW +14c to 6.33 on Black Sea risk (Ukraine strike on the Crimea bridge); Jan beans −4c to ~12.26; Dec corn −2c to ~4.47
Wheat price action is still poor. The summer lows have been taken out, and the Black Sea hasn’t added any US wheat demand
Corn: 4.57 is the line in the sand. A break below 4.38 targets the 4.2575 summer low
Beans are under pressure from the weak BRL and a US crush pace lagging USDA’s projection
No fund-positioning data was given
Ukraine’s ag minister: 2027 grain could fall to ~30 MMT from 62 (corn 12–14 vs 29–30; wheat ~17)
Post-war vs pre-war: Russian wheat +18.3%, corn ~+13%; Ukraine wheat −14.4%, corn −5%
Joe: the Black Sea story keeps failing to move price
Favorable weather is weighing on beans. No significant Brazil problem yet (early)
Tue: live cattle −1.43 to −2.60; feeders −1.80 to −6.38. Cattle on Feed report is due Friday
NAHB HMI −4 to 25, the lowest since Apr 2020. 46% of builders are cutting prices and 68% are offering incentives
30y mortgage ~7.1% (Freddie Mac) vs ~5.5% on the 30y Treasury
Fed: the script blamed equity weakness on “more aggressive Fed rate hikes” (verify, may be a misstatement)
Equities Tue: Nasdaq −2.5% (lowest since April), S&P −1.9%. NVDA ~−36% from its October high; Q3 net income was $65.3B and its Q4 guidance beat consensus
This morning: S&P +0.4%, Treasuries mixed, crude −0.91 at 85.10

flags: They called the housing index both a “14-year low” and the lowest since Apr 2020, which don’t match
NVDA forward P/E was given as “10.8” vs 18.3 for the S&P, which looks wrong
